OpenAI made a move this week that every CTO and every consulting firm should be watching closely.

The company launched an OpenAI-controlled Deployment Company with 19 partner firms and acquired Tomoro — bringing in 150 forward-deployed engineers. Translation: OpenAI is no longer just building AI models. It is now in the business of deploying them inside your organization.

This collapses a boundary that has defined the AI industry until now. Model providers built capabilities. Consulting firms and internal teams handled implementation. OpenAI just inserted itself between the model and your production workflows — the exact position where switching costs compound and long-term lock-in takes root.

For CTOs, the build-vs-buy calculation just changed. When your model provider also owns your deployment relationship, every integration makes it harder to switch. For systems integrators, this is a direct competitive incursion from a company that also controls the underlying technology.

The broader pattern is clear. AI companies are moving downstream into implementation. They are not waiting for enterprises to figure out deployment. They are owning it — and capturing the value.
